title: Percentage and decimal equivalents
keyIdea: A fraction, a decimal and a per cent can name the same amount. To switch between them, make the fraction into hundredths. 1/5 is 20/100, so 1/5 = 20% = 0.2. Then 2/5 = 40% = 0.4 and 4/5 = 80% = 0.8. 1/2 = 50% = 0.5, 1/4 = 25% = 0.25 and 3/4 = 75% = 0.75. Fractions with a bottom number of 20, 25 or 50 scale up the same way: multiply the top and the bottom by the same number until the bottom is 100, so 7/25 = 28/100 = 28%. To find a per cent of an amount, use its fraction: 40% of 60 is 2/5 of 60, which is 24.
familyTip: When you see a sale sign, turn the per cent into a fraction together. 25% off is a quarter off, 20% off is a fifth off. Work out the money taken off, then what you would pay.

visual.caption: Which amount is each card the same as? Drag each card to a box, or tap it and then a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: shade fifths of 100 squares, scale to hundredths, line up fractions with decimals and per cents, find 40% of 60, pay sale prices.

kid: Per cent means out of 100. A strip of 100 little squares cut into 5 equal parts has 20 squares in each part. So one fifth is 20 out of 100. That is 20%, and as a decimal it is 0.2.

Two fifths is 40 squares, so 2/5 = 40% = 0.4. Four fifths is 80 squares, so 4/5 = 80% = 0.8. Watch out: 1/5 is not 5%, and 1/4 is not 0.4. The bottom number tells you how many parts, not the digits of the answer.

Some fractions have 20, 25 or 50 on the bottom. Make the bottom 100. For 7/25, times 25 by 4 to get 100. Times the top by 4 too, so you get 28/100. That is 28%, or 0.28. If you only change the bottom, the amount gets smaller.
To find a per cent of a number, use its fraction. 40% of 60 is 2/5 of 60. One fifth of 60 is 12, so two fifths is 24. In a sale, 25% off £40 means a quarter, £10, is taken off. You pay the rest: £30.
adult: Ages 9 to 10. The National Curriculum in England for Year 5 asks pupils to 'solve problems which require knowing percentage and decimal equivalents of 1/2, 1/4, 1/5, 2/5, 4/5 and those fractions with a denominator of a multiple of 10 or 25'. It builds on the Year 5 statement that per cent means 'number of parts per hundred', and Year 6 uses it to find percentages of amounts and to compare across fractions, decimals and percentages.

The lab keeps one model in view: hundredths. Children shade fifths on a strip of 100 squares, scale 3/20, 7/25 and 9/50 to hundredths by multiplying the numerator and denominator by the same number, place six key fractions on a 0 to 1 line beside their decimal and per cent, find 40% of 60 by cutting the amount into fifths or tenths, and take 25% and 20% off two prices.

Common mistakes. Children often copy the digits of a fraction into a decimal (1/4 = 0.4, 1/5 = 0.5 or 5%). Some change only the denominator to 100 (7/25 = 7%). Others subtract the per cent from the amount (40% of 60 = 20), divide by the per cent (25% of 80 = 80 ÷ 25), or give the discount when the question asks for the sale price. Asking 'how many hundredths is that?' fixes most of these.

practice.prompt: What is 2/5 as a per cent?
practice.hint: One fifth of 100 is 20. How many hundredths are two fifths?
practice.explain: 1/5 = 20/100, so 2/5 = 40/100 = 40%. 25% is a quarter, and 20% is only one fifth.

practice.prompt: What is {a}/25 as a per cent? (Type the number only.)
practice.hint: What do you multiply 25 by to make 100? Do the same to the top.

practice.prompt: Which decimal is the same as 3/4?
practice.hint: 3/4 is three quarters. How many hundredths is one quarter?
practice.explain: One quarter is 25/100, so three quarters is 75/100 = 0.75. 0.34 just copies the digits.

practice.hint: 20% is the same as 1/5. Split {=a*5} into 5 equal parts.

practice.prompt: A £40 bag has 25% off. What is the sale price?
practice.hint: 25% is a quarter. Find a quarter of £40, then take it away.
practice.explain: A quarter of £40 is £10, which is the amount off. You pay £40 − £10 = £30. £15 comes from 40 − 25.

pool.hint: 0.8 is 8 tenths, or 80 hundredths. Which fraction is 80 out of 100?

pool.prompt: What is {a}/20 as a per cent? (Type the number only.)
What is {a}/50 as a per cent? (Type the number only.)

pool.hint: 25% is a quarter. Split {=a*4} into 4 equal parts.

pool.prompt: Sam says 1/5 = 0.5 because there is a 5. What is 1/5 as a decimal?
pool.hint: Share 100 into 5 equal parts. How many hundredths in each?
pool.explain: 100 ÷ 5 = 20, so 1/5 = 20/100 = 0.2. The 5 counts the parts; it is not a digit of the decimal.

pool.hint: What times 25 makes 100? Use it on both numbers.
pool.explain: 25 × 4 = 100 and 9 × 4 = 36, so 9/25 = 36/100 = 36%. 9% changes only the bottom number.

pool.hint: 40% is 2/5. Find one fifth of 30 first.
pool.explain: One fifth of 30 is 6, so two fifths is 12. 10 comes from 30 − 20 and is not linked to 40%.

pool.prompt: Trainers cost £60 with 20% off. How much is taken off?
pool.hint: 20% is one fifth. The question asks what is taken off, not what you pay.
pool.explain: One fifth of £60 is £12, so £12 is taken off. £48 is what you pay; £40 comes from 60 − 20.

pool.hint: Write each one as hundredths first.
